pr_title: Fix crash when creating collections named "All beatmaps" or "Manage collections..."
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/25834

The name fallback that was there previously since https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/11892 was half broken. This way should be a lot less prone to failure.

issue_context.title: Crash after creating collection called "All beatmaps"
issue_context.body:
### Type

Crash to desktop

### Bug description

Discovered while trying to break things to find edge case bugs. Causes hard crash and prevents game from moving past main menu after reopening.

Steps to reproduce: right click map to add to new collection -> create new collection called "All beatmaps" -> crash

Terminal crash output:

Unhandled exception. System.ArgumentException: The item osu.Game.Collections.CollectionFilterMenuItem already exists in this Dropdown.
   at osu.Framework.Graphics.UserInterface.Dropdown`1.addDropdownItem(T value, Nullable`1 position)
   at osu.Framework.Graphics.UserInterface.Dropdown`1.collectionChanged(Object sender, NotifyCollectionChangedEventArgs e)
   at osu.Framework.Bindables.BindableList`1.addRange(IList items, HashSet`1 appliedInstances)
   at osu.Framework.Bindables.BindableList`1.addRange(IList items, HashSet`1 appliedInstances)
   at osu.Framework.Bindables.BindableList`1.AddRange(IEnumerable`1 items)
   at osu.Game.Collections.CollectionDropdown.collectionsChanged(IRealmCollection`1 collections, ChangeSet changes) in /home/runner/work/osu-auth-client/osu-auth-client/osu/osu.Game/Collections/CollectionDropdown.cs:line 70
   at Realms.NotificationCallbacks`1.Notify(ChangeSet changes, Boolean shallow)
   at Realms.RealmCollectionBase`1.Realms.INotifiable<Realms.NotifiableObjectHandleBase.CollectionChangeSet>.NotifyCallbacks(Nullable`1 changes, Boolean shallow)
   at Realms.NotifiableObjectHandleBase.NotifyObjectChanged(IntPtr managedHandle, CollectionChangeSet* changes, Boolean shallow)

### Screenshots or videos

_No response_

### Version

2023.1218.0

### Logs

[shorter_runtime.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/13702731/shorter_runtime.log)

review_comments: scary but i'll assume there's some theory behind this.

The way to think about it is as such: if two objects are equal, they must have the same hash code, but two objects with the same hash code are not necessarily equal.

So a constant hash code spec such as this ensures that all instances of the class have the same hash code, and since the equality member only checks type, this satisfies the first part.

There is no actual data to base the hash code implementation on. If anything it'll just be a little inefficient in a dictionary, but the assumption is that there's only ever going to be one of these per dropdown.
